ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Orderly removal without prominent inflammation

A biopsy shows scattered shrunken cells divided into membrane-bound fragments. Adjacent macrophages promptly engulf these fragments, and little inflammation surrounds them despite clear evidence of cell death. Which feature best explains the limited inflammatory response?

  1. Intracellular enzymes are released freely
  2. The affected cells continue normal proliferation
  3. All mitochondrial proteins remain unchanged
  4. Neutrophils digest a large extracellular tissue cavity
  5. Cell contents remain contained during rapid clearance
Answer and explanation

Cell contents remain contained during rapid clearance

Packaging into apoptotic bodies and prompt phagocytosis limit exposure of inflammatory intracellular contents.

Option explanations

Cell contents remain contained during rapid clearance: Packaging into apoptotic bodies and prompt phagocytosis limit exposure of inflammatory intracellular contents.

Intracellular enzymes are released freely: Free leakage of intracellular contents is more typical of necrosis and promotes inflammation.

The affected cells continue normal proliferation: The cells are dying rather than proliferating.

All mitochondrial proteins remain unchanged: Mitochondrial signaling may be involved despite the limited inflammation.

Neutrophils digest a large extracellular tissue cavity: A neutrophil-rich cavity describes an abscess rather than scattered apoptosis.
